newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico grants first natgas permit to Midcon.
newsitem.headline: Mexico grants first natgas permit to Midcon.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) said on Thursday it had granted MidCon Gas Natural de Mexico SA de CV the first natural gas transportation permit under a government privatisation plan.
MidCon, a subsidiary of Occidental Petroleum Corp, was the first company to apply for a transportation permit, the CRE said.
"This company runs the most important long-distance pipeline in the United States and supplies about 10 percent of the total current demand in this country," the CRE said.

The CRE said MidCon would invest almost $50 million in the construction of a pipeline 62 km (100 miles) long that will transport natural gas from Ciudad Aleman near the U.S. border to Monterrey, a major city in northern Mexico.
"The pipeline capacity is 270 million cubic feet per day without compression and will fulfil the energy needs of one of the most important gas-consuming cities in the country," the CRE said.
The permit will enable MidCon to transport gas for 30 renewable years, and construction of the pipeline should start within the next six months, the CRE said.
